title: The third golden age of software engineering – thanks to AI, with Grady Booch
summary: Grady Booch frames AI coding as another rise in abstraction like compilers, argues software engineering is more than coding, and rejects claims it will be automated within a year.

verdicts.note: Prediction tracked against 2026 reality: agents handle more scoped tasks, but end-to-end engineering (requirements, review, operations) still depends on people; METR horizons and hiring data don't support 'most or all' yet.

assertions.quote: Your tools are changing, but your problems are not.

verdicts.note: Through 2026 evidence points to role change and slower junior hiring, not elimination of the profession; long-run is uncertain.

assertions.quote: focus upon the fundamentals because those skills are never going to go away

verdicts.note: DORA 2025 found AI amplifies existing engineering practices; strong fundamentals predict AI benefit.

assertions.quote: He's leading a company who needs to make money and it's a company who he needs to speak to his stakeholders.

verdicts.note: Labs do have incentives and many evals are self-reported, but independent evals (METR, SWE-bench, LMArena) largely confirm capability gains.

assertions.quote: We're going to see more software written by people who are not professionals.

verdicts.note: Tools like Lovable, v0, Replit let non-developers produce working prototypes; widely observed.

assertions.quote: English is a good enough programming language much like Cobalt was

verdicts.note: A framing of how software is built rather than a testable factual claim; widely adopted as a lens.

assertions.quote: this only works in those circumstances where I'm doing something that people have done hundreds and hundreds of times before

verdicts.note: Benchmarks and field studies show strong performance on well-specified, common tasks and weaker results on context-heavy, novel logic.

assertions.quote: move up a level of abstraction start worrying about systems

verdicts.note: Humans still own constraints and tradeoffs, but models can now propose reasonable designs when given context; the gap is narrowing.

assertions.quote: I who know those fundamentals can begin nudging and cleaning out the pieces

verdicts.note: Studies show novices accept incorrect AI code more often; verifying output requires domain and code literacy.

assertions.quote: about 90% of it maybe in a year and then more and we thought that's silly and then he was right

verdicts.note: Industry-wide, AI did not write ~90% of code by late 2025; but some AI-heavy teams (including at Anthropic) reported 70-90%+, so it partly came true in narrow settings.

assertions.quote: We are moving up a level of abstraction much like what happened in the rise from machine language to assembly language

verdicts.note: A historical framing; the analogy is debated because LLM output is non-deterministic, unlike compilers.
